local_market_context: A Vancouver therapy search often starts with a place and a concern together: a counsellor in Kitsilano, trauma therapy downtown, couples counselling in North Vancouver, or an online counsellor licensed in British Columbia. People also filter by approach, cost, availability and whether the clinician works with children, teens or adults. A homepage that stops at “therapy in Vancouver” leaves most of that intent unanswered.

We map those routes and build pages for them: a plain-spoken homepage, specialty pages, and a location or service-area page covering the neighbourhoods and Lower Mainland communities the practice actually serves. Links between those pages and the booking information make the next step obvious.

We also remove friction for search engines: navigation that can be crawled, headings that use Vancouver and British Columbia accurately, mobile layouts that load quickly, and titles and descriptions that reflect the page. The result is a site that describes the practice clearly rather than repeating a city name.

ai.heading: What an AI search optimization agency does for Vancouver therapists
paragraphs: Ask an AI assistant for a trauma counsellor in Vancouver, or a couples therapist near Mount Pleasant or North Vancouver, and the reply is built from sources the tool can read and trust. Clear, consistent pages give it the material it needs: who the clinician helps, where they are registered in British Columbia, what they specialise in and how to arrange a first session.

AI search optimization, or AI SEO, is the work of making a practice understood and cited by those systems. AEO, answer engine optimization, focuses on direct answers that can be lifted from a page. GEO, generative engine optimization, is about consistent, accurate descriptions across the sources AI tools consult. You can read more about our AI search optimization services.

These labels describe overlapping parts of the same SEO discipline, not a separate product with a different guarantee. Nobody can promise a citation or a position in an AI answer. What we can do is make the facts about your Vancouver practice easy to find, quote and repeat.

In Vancouver, a search might be framed around Kitsilano or Mount Pleasant, a BC registration, a specific approach, or a clinician who sees clients online across the Lower Mainland. People increasingly put those questions to ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and Perplexity, which assemble a shortlist from practice sites, directories and profiles rather than a single map result.

We make the practice legible to those systems by fixing inconsistent addresses and service areas, publishing specialties and populations in plain language, adding structured data, and answering the questions that precede a first call. Generative engine optimization, or GEO, is the ongoing work of keeping those descriptions aligned; it is not a promise of placement.

faq_heading: AI search optimization and GEO questions from Vancouver therapists

faqs.q: Can a solo practice rank for “counsellor Vancouver”?
faqs.a: A solo practice can compete for Vancouver searches when the site is clear about the work it does and the communities it serves. Google rewards focused specialty pages, a complete Google Business Profile, genuine reviews and a fast mobile site. We pursue realistic searches rather than promising a position.

faqs.q: Is SEO useful if all sessions are online?
faqs.a: Yes. People still search for a British Columbia-registered counsellor, a specific specialty or a clinician who offers telehealth from Vancouver. The site should explain that sessions are online, which parts of BC you serve and what the first appointment involves.

faqs.q: Should the site mention Kitsilano, Mount Pleasant, Burnaby or Surrey?
faqs.a: Name the places the practice genuinely serves on the office or service-area page. A clear service-area section is more useful than a thin duplicate page for every neighbourhood. If a nearby city produces real demand, it may deserve its own page later, but not one that repeats the same copy.

No timeline is promised. Google sets the pace, and rankings depend on the starting site, the competition, the review profile and how consistently the work is maintained. The first visible progress is the work itself — fixes, new pages and rewritten titles — followed by reporting on the searches the pages appear for.

The work is priced as a 3-month implementation project. The three packages are Starter ($329.99/month), Professional ($379.99/month) and Premium ($429.99/month), paid across a 12-month plan. Each monthly amount is an installment toward the project rather than an ongoing retainer. A larger group practice may need a broader scope, which we confirm in writing after a free review.

faqs.q: Do you work with group practices?
faqs.a: Yes. A group practice usually needs a clearer structure: who each clinician is, which specialties and populations they serve, where sessions happen and how inquiries are routed. We plan around the group as a whole without losing the individual clinicians a client may be looking for.

faqs.q: Does your marketing respect British Columbia licensing bodies and professional ethics rules?
faqs.a: We avoid guarantees, clinical claims and misleading wording. Marketing should describe the practice accurately, not promise a ranking or an outcome. The practice remains responsible for its own compliance with BC regulatory bodies and professional obligations, and we flag anything that may need a closer review.

faqs.q: What is AI search optimization (AI SEO, AEO, GEO) for therapists?
faqs.a: It is the practice of making a therapy practice legible to AI tools: accurate, consistent details about specialties, registration, location and booking, written clearly on the site and across profiles. AEO (answer engine optimization) and GEO (generative engine optimization) describe parts of the same work. Nobody can promise a citation or a position in an AI answer.

faqs.q: Do Vancouver clients use AI tools like ChatGPT to choose a therapist?
faqs.a: Some do, especially when they want a specialty, a language or a BC-registered clinician and do not want to open ten tabs. Assistants summarise what they can verify. A practice with clear pages and consistent directory details gives them more to work with, though no agency can guarantee an answer.
